Prior distributions for drmTMB models

Source: R/prior.R
priors.Rd

Prior distributions for the prior argument of drmTMB. With priors, the estimates are the posterior mode (maximum a posteriori), and the standard errors are from the curvature of the log posterior, see drmTMB.

Usage

negate(p)

normal(mean = 0, sd = 1)

student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1)

lognormal(meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1)

pert(min, mode, max, shape = 4)

half_normal(scale = 1)

half_student_t(df = 3, scale = 1)

Arguments

p

a prior, for negate

mean, sd

mean and standard deviation of the normal distribution

df

degrees of freedom of the Student t distribution

location, scale

location and scale of the Student t distribution, or scale of the half normal and half Student t distributions

meanlog, sdlog

mean and standard deviation of the log of a lognormal parameter

min, mode, max

minimum, mode and maximum of the PERT distribution

shape

the shape (weight of the mode) of the PERT distribution

Value

a drcprior object, for the argument prior of drmTMB

Details

The priors are given by name in prior=list(...) of drmTMB: b1-b5, coefficient names, "bmd" (with bmdpar), "sd" for the standard deviations of the random effects, "sigma", "phi" or "theta" for the residual parameter, and the parameters of correlation structures and variance functions; see the argument prior of drmTMB. The prior lognormal() is not related to family="lognormal" or model="lognormal".

  • normal(mean, sd): normal distribution.

  • student_t(df, location, scale): Student t distribution with df degrees of freedom, shifted by location and scaled by scale.

  • lognormal(meanlog, sdlog): lognormal distribution of a positive parameter, with log(parameter) normal with mean meanlog and standard deviation sdlog.

  • pert(min, mode, max, shape): the PERT distribution of EFSA (2022) for benchmark dose modelling, a beta distribution on (min, max) with mode mode and the shape parameters 1 + shape (mode - min)/(max - min) and 1 + shape (max - mode)/(max - min); shape = 4 by default.

  • half_normal(scale), half_student_t(df, scale): normal and Student t distributions folded at 0, for standard deviations.

  • negate(p): the prior p of the negative of the parameter, e.g. b3=negate(lognormal(1, 1)) for a negative steepness b3 (a decreasing curve) whose absolute value is lognormal.

A prior whose support is wider than the range of the parameter, e.g. a normal prior for a parameter bounded below by 0, is truncated to that range and renormalised; the normalisation does not change the estimates, but enters the marginal likelihood of marglik.

See also

drmTMB, efsapriors, fitpert, marglik

Examples

normal(8, 1)
#> normal(8, 1) 
pert(0.5, 3, 10)
#> pert(0.5, 3, 10) 
half_normal(1)
#> half_normal(1) 
# posterior modes with priors on the upper asymptote, the ED50 and the residual standard deviation
pmod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
               start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE),
               prior = list(b2 = normal(8, 1), b4 = pert(0.5, 3, 10), sigma = half_normal(1)))
summary(pmod)
#> Call:
#> drmTMB(form = rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, start = c(b1 = 0, 
#>     b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE), model = "loglogistic", 
#>     prior = list(b2 = normal(8, 1), b4 = pert(0.5, 3, 10), sigma = half_normal(1)))
#> 
#> Model:  loglogistic, decreasing curve
#> Family: gaussian, identity link for the asymptotes
#> 
#> Number of observations: 24
#> Log-likelihood: -18.61 (df = 4), AIC: 45.22, BIC: 49.93
#> 
#> Priors:
#>   b2 ~ normal(8, 1)
#>   b4 ~ pert(0.5, 3, 10)
#>   sigma ~ half_normal(1)
#> 
#> Coefficients (posterior modes):
#>                Estimate Std. Error
#> b2:(Intercept)    7.862      0.191
#> b3:(Intercept)   -2.467      0.323
#> b4:(Intercept)    3.259      0.185
#> Fixed: b1:(Intercept) = 0, b5:(Intercept) = 0
#> 
#> Residual standard deviation: 0.5333
#> 
#> Optimiser: nlminb: both X-convergence and relative convergence (5), maximum absolute gradient 3.4e-07
